To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

model checking techniques can be applied successfully to model-based design of real-time embedded software and that the behavioral hierarchy of the design is an important factor in the efficiency of model checking.

(i) the behavioral hierarchy inherent in the model-based design of embedded software provides opportunities for exploiting model checking techniques, (ii) model checking of the behavioral hierarchy is more efficient than checking the flat model, and (iii) the model checking of a behavioral hierarchy can be done in a modular way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of model checking techniques for the verification of high-level models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research is very interesting and promising, however it is not clear how the results can be used in practice.
the model checking techniques have been applied successfully to hardware and software systems, and the model checking technology is now mature and ready for industrial applications.
model based design is a good approach for software development, and model checking is a good approach to software verification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a model-based design framework for software systems that is based on a hierarchical decomposition of system behavior, and we have developed efficient model checking techniques for this framework.
we have developed a new approach for model checking based on exploiting behavioral hierarchy in models.
we have developed a model checking framework for Statecharts, which has been applied to the verification of a variety of real-life systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hierarchical structure of models, as opposed to the flatness of code, can be exploited for efficient model checking.
model checking techniques can be applied efficiently to high-level models.
model checking can be applied to large-scale models if we take advantage of a behavioral hierarchy in models.
